newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks rebound on bargain-hunting, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks rebound on bargain-hunting, trade thin.

text.p: Tokyo stocks recovered sharply on Wednesday after the previous day's tumble.
Brokers said that while there were no supportive news in the market, worries about Tuesday's stock price falls triggered bargain-hunting and short-covering in thin trade.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 average closed up 387.70 points or 2.02 percent at 19,549.41. It had fallen 528.75 points or 2.69 percent to a 12-month low of 19,161.71 on Tuesday. March Nikkei futures finished up 280 at 19,530.

Last week, the government decided to raise the consumption tax in April and end special income tax cuts from January, sparking fears that these measures may hurt the fledgling recovery, brokers said. The market has been also discouraged by a delay in a corporate tax cut, which had been proposed to support domestic business activities.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's "Big Bang" reform plan to liberalize the nation's financial markets and increase competition among financial institutions by 2001 has also put pressure on Japanese financial institutions, which are still struggling to dispose of bad asset problems, some brokers said.
However, Nomura Securities' strategist Masaaki Higashida said there were no real reasons to trigger the recent sell-off.

"If the Nikkei fell below the psychological barrier of 19,000, the scene would probably change dramatically," he said. While the Nikkei hovers above 19,000, the recent selling may be described as technical selling caused by unwinding of long margin trading positions and long futures positions, he added.
Higashida said that he expected the Nikkei to move between 19,000 and 20,500 over the coming week.
The broader TOPIX index closed up 20.98 points or 1.45 percent at 1,469.43, while the Nikkei 300 average rose 4.53 points or 1.65 percent to 279.89.
Gaining shares outnumbered losers with 794 issues higher, 320 issues lower and 152 unchanged.
Advanced sectors were led by the securities, telecommunication, rubber, precision instruments and drug sectors, while there were no major declining sectors.
Toyota Motor shares recovered, closing up 80 yen at 3,260 yen. Investors were bargain-hunting blue-chip shares such as Toyota, brokers said.
